data.why: These are the repository's own demo scene/package JSON files referenced by the Custom/README.md as editable examples to upload through the tool's file inputs.

goals: Build a custom test-pattern scene from standardized entities (grille, dot array, checkerboard, bullseye, circle, plane, triangle, gradient, text) to target a specific display characteristic (resolution, chromatic aberration, color mapping)
Load an existing/demo pattern or package JSON file, inspect and edit its entities, and confirm it renders as expected in the in-browser preview
Group several patterns into an ordered package/scene list so the same set can be stepped through on a headset for side-by-side comparison
Export/save the edited pattern or package as a JSON file so it can be re-opened, shared with a collaborator, or run on a different headset
Upload a custom texture image onto a plane entity and verify it displays with correct aspect ratio and color

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose well (building, ordering and saving standard test-pattern packages so headsets can be compared on the same scene), and its building, animation and ordering tasks are solid and mostly backed by the screens. But it leaves out the other half of portability, loading a shared package and showing it on a headset, along with the blocked package-creation steps, so it needs those nodes and a few merges before filing.
